clips.send: Someone forwards it to a friend who still hangs around people dragging them down - shame they can't ignore, now that the pattern's obvious.
clips.caption:
One rule. The richest man alive, at the time, said it mattered more than anything else.

Aristotle Onassis - the Greek shipping magnate who later married Jackie Kennedy - said the single most important factor in success is who you associate with. Associate with losers, you become a loser. Associate with winners, it rubs off.

Kevin Trudeau says his own mother used to get furious at him as a kid for listening to motivational tapes by self-made millionaires. "Keep listening to those people," she'd warn, "and you're going to turn out just like them."

His response: that's the point.

Who have you been letting rub off on you?

clips.send: A friend sends it to someone who keeps complaining about the same problem for years without fixing it - shame they can't shake.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau was sitting on a porch in Macon, Georgia, sipping iced tea, when an old hound dog lying nearby kept letting out a little howl, putting its head back down, then howling again a few minutes later.

"What's wrong with your dog?" he asked. "Oh," his friend said, "he's sleeping on a nail." "Why doesn't he move, then?" Kevin asked.

"It doesn't hurt him that much."

That's most people's entire relationship with the thing holding them back. Not painful enough to actually get up and move - just painful enough to howl about it every few minutes, for years.

What nail are you still lying on?
